risk_if_not_implemented: Without Secure Practices Alignment Justification, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Authorization / Certification / License (R-EX-11), Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides third-party oversight and contractual controls that compensates for the absence of Secure Practices Alignment Justification (GOV-03.1) by extending security obligations and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct primary control implementation. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Control Objectives
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to establish control objectives as the basis for the design, selection, implementation and management of the organization's internal security, compliance and resilience control system.
compensating_control_2.justification: Control Objectives (GOV-03.3) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Secure Practices Alignment Justification (GOV-03.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
